mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy regime that increases discount rates for equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the average forward return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% signals tightening labor market conditions that increase wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive policy and suppressing equity valuations over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases when UNRATE falls below 4.5%, or the mean forward return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction permits above 1.2 million units signals strong household demand and confidence, which drives consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances despite HOUST above 1.2 million, or the average forward return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production and rise in the unemployment rate signals a weakening manufacturing sector and labor market contraction, indicating an imminent economic slowdown that reduces corporate profitability and triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases when both INDPRO < 114.0 and UNRATE > 4.6%, or the joint signal fails to produce a statistically significant negative return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the CPIAUCSL above 208.5 with a 12-month increase exceeding 3.5% signals persistent inflationary pressure, increasing the likelihood of further rate hikes and raising equity discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 208.5 and 12mo_change > 3.5%, or the average forward return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above 380 billion dollars signals strong consumer demand, which supports corporate revenues and earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances despite RSAFS above 380 billion, or the average forward return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in payroll employment and decline in the unemployment rate signals a robust labor market that increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive policy and suppressing equity valuations over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases when PAYEMS > 138000 and UNRATE < 4.8%, or the joint signal fails to produce a statistically significant negative return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP growth above 2.0% annualized in the most recent quarter signals strong aggregate demand and economic momentum, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances despite GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized, or the average forward return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
